anomalies.observed: Two 10K pull-up resistors sit side by side on the top-right of the root sheet: R3 is tied to the +5V logic rail, but R6 is tied to the VCC rail (the same rail that feeds the input of U1, the LM1117-5.0 regulator, and the P-FET source/JP1). Both resistors' lower terminals carry the same 5V-domain signal (tach/reset-class net).
anomalies.expected: All pull-ups on 5V logic signals (tach input, reset, I2C lines) must reference the regulated +5V rail. VCC is by definition higher than +5V (it is the LM1117 input that is regulated down to +5V), so it must not be used to pull up a 5V logic pin.

evidence.quote: Root sheet, top right: R3 10K with a +5V power flag on top; R6 10K with a VCC power flag on top, both feeding a 5V-domain label net.
Page 2: U1 LM1117-5.0 — pin 3 'VCC' (input), pin 2 '+5V' (output), pin 1 GND.

anomalies.impact: The 5V logic node (tach/reset) is pulled toward the unregulated VCC rail. The ATtiny pin's clamp diode will conduct continuously, the logic level will be pulled above the MCU supply, and the input can misread or be damaged; the same VCC and +5V rails are also softly bridged through the two 10K resistors.

parsed.summary: The schematic shows a 5V-domain pull-up (R6, 10K) tied to the VCC pre-regulator rail while its companion pull-up (R3, 10K) correctly references +5V, which over-voltages the associated logic net; apart from this the ATtiny fan-controller architecture (LM1117-5.0, pot/tach/PWM, ISP, high-side P-FET switch) reads as intended.
